To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and validated a robust, rapid, accurate, and low-cost method to simultaneously genotype 16 mitochondrial coding region SNPs, including 7 SNPs in the HVR1, 8 SNPs in the coding region and the 9-bp deletion (9-bp del) in the tRNALeu(UUR) gene.
a set of 17 mtDNA coding region SNPs can be simultaneously genotyped in a single SNaPshot multiplex reaction and that the methodology is robust and reliable for forensic and anthropological studies.
we have developed a robust multiplex assay for mtDNA SNP genotyping based on SNaPshot technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a fast and accurate multiplexed SNP typing assay for forensic and anthropological purposes, which could be easily adapted to other mtDNA coding regions of forensic or phylogenetic interest.
the development of new methodologies to simultaneously genotype mtDNA coding region SNPs, and the validation of a multiplex SNaPshot assay for forensic and anthropological applications.
the development of a rapid and robust multiplex assay for the simultaneous typing of mtDNA coding region SNPs that will facilitate both forensic and anthropological studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SNaPshot multiplex reaction described here is a fast, accurate, and robust tool to genotype mtDNA coding region SNPs in forensic and anthropological studies.
this multiplex SNaPshot approach provides a powerful and rapid alternative to the current mitochondrial analysis in forensic and anthropological fields.
this new method represents a powerful tool for the forensic, anthropological, and population geneticist.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a rapid and robust method for the simultaneous typing of 17 mtDNA coding region SNPs, which allows us to allocate West Eurasian mtDNA haplotypes into the corresponding branches of the mtDNA skeleton and also to increase considerably the discrimination capacity of current mtDNA analysis in the forensic area.

the set of SNPS described in this work can be used to genotype 17 coding region positions in a single multiplex reaction, with a total reaction time of 2h 30 min, using only 0.2 ng of DNA and 5 microl of reaction mixture.
we have developed a fast, robust and cost-effective method that is able to simultaneously type 17 coding region mtDNA SNPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the SNaPshot technology with the selection of appropriate polymorphic positions can be successfully used as a fast and cost-effective tool for mtDNA typing.
this method is an efficient tool that allows a fast and accurate identification of mitochondrial haplotypes in forensic and anthropological samples.
SNaPshot can be a valuable tool for the rapid and accurate genotyping of a set of mtDNA SNPs in forensic and anthropological applications.
